author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Capture useful before-and-after graphics evidence
summary: Match serial, camera, animation frame, renderer, driver, resolution, and one tested variable; keep lossless captures with readable metadata and reject pairs whose timing, crop, color pipeline, or game state changed.
heroAlt: Official PCSX2 side-by-side graphics comparison showing matched before and after frames

blocks.text: Change one variable and preserve one frame

A useful comparison allows another person to attribute the visible difference without guessing. Fix the camera, game state, animation moment, serial, renderer, driver, resolution, aspect, and display pipeline. Name the single changed variable, such as blending tier, API, patch, or driver. Use direct lossless capture rather than a photograph unless the external display is the subject.
Two attractive screenshots are not evidence when their camera, time of day, motion frame, crop, or settings differ. Recapture instead of explaining away uncontrolled changes.

items: Normal in-game save before a controllable static or scripted moment.
Complete before-profile and after-profile exports.
Serial, revision, build, driver, API, resolution, and aspect labels.
Lossless or high-quality direct capture path.
A naming convention that links images to the manifest.

blocks.text: Capture the baseline before applying the change

items: 1. Cold-boot the before profile and navigate from the normal save to the chosen moment.
2. Pause input at the defined marker or use a deterministic scripted frame.
3. Capture direct output without resizing, filters, annotations, or social-media compression.
4. Apply exactly one tested variable and restart the session when the renderer requires it.
5. Return from the same normal save and capture the matched frame.
6. Verify pixel dimensions, crop, color mode, camera, and HUD state are equal.
7. Store captions and settings outside the image so the source pixels remain available.
8. Repeat the pair when timing differs or when a second scene is needed to prove scope.

blocks.text: Matched pairs turn subjective descriptions into inspectable evidence. Keeping raw frames separate from annotated copies allows zoom and pixel comparison without text covering the fault. A manifest prevents filenames such as final2-fixed-new from losing technical meaning.
A reviewer should identify the tested variable from metadata and see no uncontrolled visual change.

items: Both images have identical dimensions, crop, aspect, and color pipeline.
Camera and animation moment match closely enough for the defect.
Only one graphics, driver, or patch variable changed.
Raw lossless frames and a readable manifest are retained.
A second person can describe the result without asking which settings were used.
Camera or game time changed: reload and recapture.
One image was recompressed or sharpened: return to raw direct output.
Multiple fixes were enabled together: rebuild isolated profiles.
HDR tone mapping differs: capture both under one documented pipeline.

blocks.text: Recreate the before profile from its export

Restore the baseline profile, cold-boot the normal save, and confirm the original frame can still be reproduced. Archive failed pairs outside the reviewed set so they cannot be mistaken for accepted evidence.
Public screenshots need a rights check

Keep captures private by default. If a report or Hub article uses an image, verify that its distribution, attribution, cropping, and download permissions are appropriate before publication. Preserve the uncropped originals beside the labeled comparison so a reviewer can inspect edges, HUD placement, and timing clues that a presentation crop may conceal. Remove personal notifications and account identifiers before sharing, but do not alter the game pixels that demonstrate the result.
